public_rationale: He made two factual points: OpenAI was 'worth' $157 billion, and it burns $5 billion or more a year. OpenAI's own announcement confirms the $157B post-money valuation from October 2024. Before the post, CNBC confirmed that OpenAI expected about $5 billion in losses on $3.7 billion of revenue in 2024. Later reports of audited figures, said to be verified by the FT, put the 2024 net loss attributable to OpenAI at $5.09 billion. That meets his '$5 billion or more'. One report said cash burn in the first half of 2024 was far lower than the net loss, because large costs did not pass through cash. But the plain reading of 'burns' in November 2024 was the widely reported annual loss. The lines about the environment, 'real meaning', and how much coverage OpenAI deserves are opinion and are not graded.
limitations: The 2024 loss figures come from press reports of company documents, not from public filings.
Under a strict cash-burn reading the result could differ. Reported first-half 2024 cash burn was much lower than the loss.
The opinion parts of the sentence were not assessed.

our_interpretation: Two factual parts can be checked: (1) OpenAI was valued at about $157 billion, and (2) OpenAI loses or burns about $5 billion or more a year.

Plain reading: in November 2024, 'burns $5 billion or more a year' pointed to the widely reported figure of about $5 billion in losses for 2024. So the test is OpenAI's annual loss for calendar 2024, the year in progress when he wrote. It is not narrowed to cash burn in any one quarter.
The remarks about the environment, 'real meaning', and how much coverage OpenAI deserves are opinion. They are not graded.
A 2024 loss of about $5 billion or more counts as support. A clearly lower annual loss, or a valuation well away from $157 billion, would count against.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable sources show OpenAI's valuation was about $157 billion in 2024, and that OpenAI's 2024 loss was about $5 billion or more.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable sources show OpenAI's 2024 annual loss was clearly below $5 billion (for example, $3 billion or less), or that the $157 billion valuation was not real.
